description: Conversion of existing first floor flat into 2 self-contained flats, involving dormer extension at rear and roof lights.
decision_conditions: The external finishing materials shall match those used in the construction of the existing building and/or areas of hard surfacing. Reason: To ensure a satisfactory appearance.

The development to which this permission relates must be begun not later than the expiration of three years beginning with the date of the decision notice.Reason: To comply with the provisions of S.51 of the Planning & Compulsory Purchase Act 2004

The development hereby permitted shall be carried out in accordance with the following approved plans: EX01EX02PL01PL02Design and Access statementEnergy Statement Reason: For the avoidance of doubt and in the interests of proper planning.

The development hereby approved shall be carried out in full accordance with the Energy Statement prepared by Beth Robinson, dated February 2026, unless otherwise submitted to and approved in writing by the local planning authority. The approved measures for reducing carbon emissions and improving energy efficiency, including but not limited to the use of low and zero carbon technologies, enhanced building fabric performance, and energy-efficient systems, shall be fully implemented prior to first occupation of the development and retained thereafterReason: In the interest of sustainable development and to ensure that the Local Planning Authority may be satisfied that CO2 emission reduction targets are met in accordance with Policy CP20 of the Enfield Core Strategy (2010), Policies DMD49, DMD50 and DMD51 of the Enfield Development Management Document (2014).

Following practical completion of works a final Energy Performance Certificate with accompanying Building Regulations compliance report shall be submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority. Where applicable, a Display Energy Certificate shall be submitted within 18 months following first occupation.Reason: In the interest of sustainable development and to ensure that the Local Planning Authority may be satisfied that CO2 emission reduction targets are met in accordance with Policy CP20 of the Enfield Core Strategy (2010), Policies DMD49, DMD50 and DMD51 of the Enfield Development Management Document (2014).

The development shall be designed and constructed to ensure that the internal consumption of potable water does not exceed 105 litres per person per day. This shall be achieved through the installation of water-efficient fittings, appliances, and, where applicable, water recycling systems. The development shall be maintained in accordance with these measures for the lifetime of the development.Reason: In the interest of sustainable development and to ensure that the Local Planning Authority may be satisfied that CO2 emission reduction targets are met in accordance with Policy CP21 of the Enfield Core Strategy (2010), Policy DMD58 of the Enfield Development Management Document (2014).

Cycle parking must be provided in compliance with the following criteria prior to occupation of the development: - Provision of a minimum of FOUR long stay cycle parking spaces (Two per unit)- In an accessible location: the access route to the cycle parking enclosures should be a minimum of 1.2m wide to enable the bike to enter the store, should be step free and involve no more than 2 doors or gates (excluding the store door) which must also have a minimum opening width of 1.2m - long stay must be secured: with a British Standard mortice lock or access fob- long stay must be fully enclosed: 4 walls and a roofReason: The Council's Climate Action and Transport Policies seek to increase the use of active and sustainable transport modes. This means that access to bicycle parking should be easy and secure to remove potential barriers to cycling.

The development shall be carried out in accordance with the approved refuse storage details as set out in  drawing PL01 before the development is occupied. The refuse storage shall be retained and maintained as such for the lifetime of the developmentReason: To ensure the provision of refuse storage in accordance with the Household Recycling and Waste Planning Guidance for New Developments (2024).
